title: Memory Care Assessments and the Care Program Billed
content:
A Larkspur memory care nurse completes cognitive and functional assessments of each Memory Care Residency Agreement resident; each assessment is recorded with its date, its type (pre-admission, post-move-in, routine, change of condition or post-hospital), its score and the care program it indicates.

## Policy

1. **Program follows the score.** Each tier is one suite type combined with one care program. The care program billed is always the program whose score band contains the most recent assessment score once its effective date has passed. The suite type does not change with the program, so a program change moves the residency to the tier with the same suite type and the new care program, at that tier's monthly rate.
2. **When reassessments fall due.**
   - A post-move-in reassessment is completed within the tier's post-move-in period of the move-in date.
   - A routine reassessment falls due once the days since the last assessment reach the tier's routine reassessment interval. The days since the last assessment are the calendar days elapsed from the most recent assessment date on the residency to the handling date.
   - A post-hospital reassessment is completed within the tier's post-hospital period of the resident's return from any hospital absence.
3. **Written program notice.** Where an assessment indicates a new care program, the written program notice is issued with the assessment record, no later than the tier's program notice period after the assessment. An assessment that indicates no change carries no program notice.
4. **Needs beyond memory care.** A score above the highest score of the advanced program's band means the resident's needs exceed what Larkspur memory care provides, and leads to the residency ending by discharge on that ground.
5. **Open residencies only.** Assessments and program changes may be recorded only while the residency is in pending admission, active, on leave or notice given status; the residency's status on the company's records decides.

## Score, band and tier: how the pieces fit

| Input | Where it comes from | What it decides |
|---|---|---|
| Most recent assessment score | The residency's assessment records | The care program, through the band that contains it |
| Suite type | The residency's current tier | Unchanged by a program change |
| Effective date of the program | The assessment, and its program notice where one is issued | From when the new program is billed |
| Tier and monthly rate | Suite type plus care program | The rate charged |

## Worked illustration (hypothetical dates)

A resident in a program whose routine interval is 90 days was last assessed on 1 February, in a year in which February has 28 days. The days since the last assessment reach 90 on 2 May, so a routine reassessment is due from that date. Had the same resident been in a program with a 60-day interval, the count would reach 60 on 2 April.

## Status test for recording

| Residency status | Assessment or program change may be recorded |
|---|---|
| Pending admission | Yes |
| Active | Yes |
| On leave | Yes |
| Notice given | Yes |
| Vacated, closed or cancelled | No |

The last row follows from the closed list in clause 5.

## Basis Q&A

**A private suite resident's score moves from the essential band into the enhanced band. Which tier is billed once the change is effective?** The private suite with the enhanced program; the suite stays private.

**Does an older assessment with a different score still count?** No. The program billed follows the most recent assessment score once its effective date has passed.
